statement: Three quarters of a class of 28 travelled by bus. How many did not travel by bus?

choices.misconception: I divided 28 by 7 instead of taking a quarter of it.
I found three quarters of 16 by mistake, mixing up the class size.
I found how many did travel by bus and gave that instead of how many did not.
I subtracted the 4 quarters as if they were 4 students.

hints: What fraction did not travel by bus?
If three quarters went by bus, the rest is one quarter. Taking one quarter of the class directly is one step; working out three quarters and subtracting is two.
One quarter of 28 is 7, so 7 students did not travel by bus.

solutions.reliable: Three quarters went by bus, so one quarter did not. One quarter of 28 is 28 divided by 4 = 7. Check the other way: three quarters is 21, and 28 - 21 = 7. The transferable idea: when a question asks about the rest, find the fraction that is left over first — it is fewer steps and fewer chances to slip.

whyOnTest: Answering with the quantity you computed rather than the one that was asked for is the single most common lost mark on the whole paper.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
